brief.title: Tujuh Triwulan: Tumbuhnya Sudah Menyalip, Ekonominya Belum?
brief.hook: Vietnam tumbuh lebih cepat dari Indonesia di tujuh triwulan terakhir. Tapi apakah PDB per kapitanya benar-benar sudah menyalip — atau cuma angka IMF yang bilang begitu?
key_points: Fokus hanya 2025-2026. Bukti utama: data triwulan aktual dari BPS (Indonesia) dan NSO/Vietnam.
Selisih pertumbuhan melebar dari ~2,2 poin (Q1 2025) menjadi ~4,5 poin (Q3 2026).
Level: BPS maupun NSO TIDAK menerbitkan PDB per kapita USD per triwulan — jadi klaim 'sudah tersalip' hanya benar untuk pertumbuhan, bukan untuk level.
Data 2025 aktual (Bank Dunia): current USD Vietnam $5.066 vs Indonesia $5.060 — selisih $6; constant 2015 USD Vietnam $4.308 vs Indonesia $4.555 — Indonesia unggul 5,7%.

Data 2026 (proyeksi): IMF WEO Oktober 2026 current USD Vietnam $5.259 vs Indonesia $5.153 (VN +2,1%); TradingEconomics constant USD $4.631 vs $4.778 (ID unggul) — basis berbeda, tidak bisa dibandingkan langsung.
Sumber lain: Macrotrends berhenti di 2025; FocusEconomics versi 2026 berbayar; countryeconomy tidak punya data Vietnam 2026. Hanya IMF yang memberi angka current-USD 2026.
Data direvisi: Q1/Q2 2026 Vietnam naik dari 7,83%/8,39% menjadi 8,15%/8,81% pada rilis Q3 2026.
Kesimpulan: tumbuhnya sudah tersalip; level per kapitanya masih photo finish dan sangat sensitif terhadap basis harga dan kurs.
brief.core_message: Selama tujuh triwulan Vietnam selalu tumbuh lebih cepat, tapi 'sudah menyalip' baru benar untuk pertumbuhan — level PDB per kapitanya masih imbang di data 2025 dan hanya diproyeksikan unggul tipis oleh IMF untuk 2026.
brief.cta: Lihat angka BPS dan NSO di layar — dan perhatikan basis harganya.
brief.tone: Informatif, berbasis bukti, transparan soal ketidakpastian data, Bahasa Indonesia percakapan
brief.target_audience: Pemirsa Indonesia yang tertarik ekonomi Asia Tenggara dan ingin melihat datanya, bukan sekadar narasi

visual_router.description: Every scene uses BOTH tools: first ~50% MoneyPrinterTurbo real footage, second ~50% Remotion animated infographic (order alternates across scenes). Continuous Gadis narration + subtitles, 0.3s crossfade at midpoint.

stat card: World Bank 2025 current USD $5,066 vs $5,060 AND constant USD $4,308 vs $4,555
stat card: IMF WEO Oct 2026 $5,259 vs $5,153 (label: PROJECTION, current USD)

metadata.data_scope: 2025-2026 quarterly growth (BPS + NSO) as primary proof; 2025 annual levels and 2026 forecasts as labeled context only
data_hierarchy: 1. BPS + NSO quarterly growth actuals - PRIMARY PROOF (growth already overtaken)
2. World Bank 2025 levels - observed context (current USD ~tie; constant USD Indonesia ahead)
3. IMF WEO Oct 2026 - PROJECTION, current USD only, must be labeled 'proyeksi'
4. TradingEconomics constant-USD - different basis, never compare directly with IMF
5. UN 2024, Macrotrends, FocusEconomics public, countryeconomy - excluded from level claims
label_rules: Every IMF number must be labeled 'proyeksi' and 'current USD' in both voice and on screen
Always state the price basis (current vs constant USD); never place IMF and TradingEconomics numbers in the same chart without a basis note
Indonesia 2025 quarterly figures rounded to 1 decimal -> show '~' approximate marker
Show revision note for Vietnam Q1/Q2 2026 (latest vintage used)
Do not claim quarterly per-capita level - agencies do not publish it

decisions.subject: Framing of the overtaking claim (growth vs level)

options_considered.label: Distinguish growth (overtaken) from level (not yet)
options_considered.reason: BPS/NSO publish quarterly growth but no quarterly per-capita USD level; 2025 levels are a dead heat and 2026 levels are projections only

options_considered.label: Claim Vietnam has overtaken outright
options_considered.rejected_because: Overstates a $6 difference and a forecast; ignores price-basis disagreement across sources

decisions.reason: Final consolidation of all findings: the only solid evidence is faster quarterly growth; the level crossover remains source- and basis-dependent.

decisions.subject: IMF vintage and cross-source comparability

options_considered.label: Use IMF WEO Oct 2026 current-USD, labeled; keep other sources separated by basis
options_considered.reason: FlareSolverr confirmed the WEO October 2026 vintage and current-price basis; TE uses constant 2015 USD and is not comparable

options_considered.label: Put IMF and TradingEconomics numbers in one chart
options_considered.rejected_because: Different price bases would produce a misleading direct comparison

decisions.reason: Locks the verified IMF vintage and enforces price-basis labeling across all visuals and narration.
